ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle LKM, LK is the upper horizontal side, and M is below; MN is perpendicular from M to LK, and there is a right-angle mark at N, so MN is the altitude to LK. Point N is on LK, and the problem gives KN = 9 and LN = 16. Point P is located on side MK, point R is located on side ML, and PR is parallel to LK. The figure also marks at M that triangle LKM is a right triangle, with the right angle at M. Reasoning: Since LN = 16 and KN = 9, LK = LN + KN = 16 + 9 = 25. For right triangle LKM, MN is the altitude from the right angle M to the hypotenuse LK. By the right triangle hypotenuse altitude theorem, the leg adjacent to KN satisfies KM^2 = KN · LK = 9 · 25 = 225, therefore KM = 15. Also, P is on MK, and PM = 2KP, so MK = PM + KP = 2KP + KP = 3KP. Thus 3KP = 15, obtaining KP = 5.

raw_record.question_text: If PR || KL, KN = 9, LN = 16, PM = 2KP, find KP.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify triangle LKM as a right triangle with the right angle at M, and identify MN as the altitude from M to hypotenuse LK, meeting LK at N. Also read that P lies on side MK between M and K. From the text, use LN = 16 and KN = 9, so LK = 25, and use PM = 2KP. Apply the right-triangle altitude-to-hypotenuse leg theorem: the leg adjacent to hypotenuse segment KN satisfies KM^2 = KN · LK = 9 · 25, so KM = 15. Since P is on MK and PM = 2KP, the whole side MK = PM + KP = 3KP. Therefore 3KP = 15 and KP = 5.

method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate setup based on the image. Place N at the origin, LK on the horizontal axis, K at (9, 0) because KN = 9, and L at (-16, 0) because LN = 16. Since the image shows MN perpendicular to LK, put M at (0, -h). Since the image shows angle LMK is a right angle, the slopes of ML and MK must multiply to -1. The slope of MK is h/9 and the slope of ML is -h/16, so their product gives -h^2/144 = -1, hence h = 12. Then KM = sqrt(9^2 + 12^2) = 15. From the image P is on MK, and from the text PM = 2KP, so MK = PM + KP = 3KP. Thus KP = 15/3 = 5.
